note: argument 0 is a bus byte; takes the semaphore at 0x3000362c with semaphore_take and a timeout argument of minus 1, logging a nonzero result at level 9; stores the result of ffe580e8 in the word at 0x3000067c+0x28; a zero bus byte returns 0 with nothing selected and the semaphore still taken; otherwise, when the callback word at +0x10 is set, calls it with the bus byte: a nonzero result runs i2c_bus_release and is returned, a zero result stores the bus byte at +1 and returns 0; with no callback logs 'I2C has no bus select' at level 1 and returns 0 with the semaphore still taken; callers ffe65b74, ffe6ca38, ffe6cdcc, ffe6ce34, ffe6cea0 and ffe6cf08; read ffe6c964-ffe6ca24

name: i2c_bus_select_probe
note: returns 0 when the word at 0x3000068c is zero; otherwise runs i2c_bus_acquire with bus byte 1 and returns its result when that is nonzero, else runs i2c_bus_release and returns 0; read ffe6ca28-ffe6ca4c

name: i2c_bus_select_call
note: argument 0 is a bus byte; calls the callback in the word at 0x3000067c+0x10 with it and returns the result, without taking the lock; with no callback logs 'I2C has no bus select' at level 1 and returns 0; read ffe6ca50-ffe6caa4

name: mbus_write_bytes
note: arguments: 0 slave address byte, 1 data pointer, 2 count (low word); calls mbus_transaction_start with initial state 2, that address, offset 0, the pointer and the count, and returns its result; the state-2 step of mbus_interrupt_step writes the data bytes without an offset byte; read ffe6cd98-ffe6cdbc

name: mbus_write_byte_locked
note: arguments: 0 bus byte, 1 slave address byte, 2 value byte; runs i2c_bus_acquire with the bus byte and returns its error when nonzero; otherwise calls mbus_write_bytes with the address, the address of the value byte in its own frame and count 1, then i2c_bus_release, and returns the transfer result; read ffe6cdc0-ffe6cdfa

name: mbus_write_register_bytes
note: arguments: 0 slave address byte, 1 register offset byte, 2 data pointer, 3 count (low word); calls mbus_transaction_start with initial state 1, the address, the offset, the pointer and the count and returns its result; the state-1 step writes the offset byte before the data; read ffe6cdfc-ffe6ce24

name: mbus_write_register_locked
note: arguments: 0 bus byte, 1 slave address byte, 2 register offset byte, 3 value byte; runs i2c_bus_acquire and returns its error when nonzero; otherwise calls mbus_write_register_bytes with the address, offset, the address of the value byte in its own frame and count 1, then i2c_bus_release, and returns the transfer result; read ffe6ce28-ffe6ce68

name: mbus_read_bytes
note: arguments: 0 slave address byte, 1 destination pointer, 2 count (low word); calls mbus_transaction_start with initial state 5, that address, offset 0, the pointer and the count and returns its result; state 5 sets bit 0 of the address byte (read) and goes straight to receive; read ffe6ce6c-ffe6ce90

name: mbus_read_byte_locked
note: arguments: 0 bus byte, 1 slave address byte, 2 destination pointer; runs i2c_bus_acquire and returns its error when nonzero; otherwise calls mbus_read_bytes with the address, the pointer and count 1, then i2c_bus_release, and returns the transfer result; read ffe6ce94-ffe6cece

name: mbus_read_register_bytes
note: arguments: 0 slave address byte, 1 register offset byte, 2 destination pointer, 3 count (low word); calls mbus_transaction_start with initial state 3, the address, offset, pointer and count and returns its result; states 3 and 4 write the offset, then repeat the start with the read bit set; read ffe6ced0-ffe6cef8

name: mbus_read_register_locked
note: arguments: 0 bus byte, 1 slave address byte, 2 register offset byte, 3 destination pointer; runs i2c_bus_acquire and returns its error when nonzero; otherwise calls mbus_read_register_bytes with the address, offset, pointer and count 1, then i2c_bus_release, and returns the transfer result; read ffe6cefc-ffe6cf3c

name: mbus_deferred_resume
note: the entry of the 'I2C_CNTL' deferred handler created by mbus_driver_init; takes the mutex at 0x300036ac (ffe4146c); when the word at 0x3000067c+0x14 (the value mbus_transaction_start stored from ffe580e8) is nonzero clears it and calls ffe40b40 with it, which returns minus 25 for a null pointer or one whose word at +0xc is not 0x5441534b, minus 20 when ffe40ee0 (called with 10 and the pointer) returns nonzero, and otherwise the result of ffe410ac on the pointer; a nonzero result is logged at level 9 with the pointer; then releases the mutex with ffe414b2; the pointer is the task that mbus_transaction_start recorded, so this reads as resuming that task, an inference; read ffe6cf40-ffe6cfa8

name: scan_port_read
note: returns the byte at MBAR+0x1c9 zero-extended, with MBAR taken from the word at 0x300002e8; read ffe72240-ffe72252

name: scan_pins_format
note: argument 0 is an output buffer; reads the byte at MBAR+0x1c9 once and passes the buffer, a format text and six characters, each '1' or '0', to format_string in this order: bit 4 (TRST), bit 3 (PSI), bit 6 (TCK), bit 5 (TMS), bit 7 (TDI), bit 0 (TDO); the text starts 'TAP values'; returns what format_string returns; read ffe72254-ffe722dc

name: scan_port_write
note: writes the low byte of argument 0 to MBAR+0x1c9; read ffe722e0-ffe722f4

name: indicator_bits_set
note: argument 0 is a mask; the table pointer is the word at 0x30000238+8 and the count the word at +0xc, in 4-byte records; for each record whose byte 2 ANDed with the mask is nonzero calls io_expander_update with byte 0 as the index and byte 1 as both mask and value, keeps a nonzero result as the return value (register d5, which is not cleared at entry, so a run with no failure returns the caller's d5), and ORs the mask into the byte at 0x30000238+2 whether or not the call failed; the table-driven output through expander bits reads as an indicator driver, which is an inference; read ffe5422c-ffe542a8

name: indicator_bits_clear
note: argument 0 is a mask; walks the same record table as indicator_bits_set; for each record whose byte 2 ANDed with the mask is nonzero calls io_expander_update with byte 0 as the index, byte 1 as the mask and value 0, keeps a nonzero result in d5 (not cleared at entry, as in indicator_bits_set), and clears the mask bits in the byte at 0x30000238+2; read ffe542ac-ffe54322

name: indicator_service
note: periodic step; returns at once when the word at 0x30000238+0x10 is zero; writes MBAR+0x43 0x55 then 0xaa (the same pair the watchdog code writes) at entry; when the countdown word at +0x14 is negative: with the byte at +1 set subtracts 1 from the word at +0x18 and, when the result is zero or below, advances the pattern (the byte at +0 becomes byte 2 of table record 1 when it equals byte 2 of record 0, otherwise byte 2 of record 0) and reloads +0x18 from the byte at +3, else just stores the decremented word; writes the pair again; if the byte at +2 ANDed with the byte at +0 is nonzero calls indicator_bits_clear with the byte at +0, else indicator_bits_set, so the bits in the byte at +0 toggle; sets the countdown to 3 (otherwise subtracts 1 from it), so the toggle step runs on every fifth call; writes the pair once more at ffe543d6 on either path before returning; the table is the one indicator_bits_set walks; read ffe54324-ffe543ee

name: indicator_pattern_set
note: arguments: 0 pattern, 1 blink period, 2 flag; calls ffe543f0 with 0xff when the flag is zero; sets the word at 0x30000238+0x10 to 1 and the byte at +4 to the pattern; when bit 2 of the pattern is set loads the byte at +0 from byte 2 of record 0 of the table at +8, sets the byte at +1 to 1 and the byte at +3 to twice the period (period below 1 counts as 1); otherwise clears the byte at +1 and loads the byte at +0 with the pattern; returns 0; read ffe54450-ffe544b6

name: io_expander_record
note: argument 0 is an index byte; the descriptor at 0x300005b8 holds a count at +4 and a table base at +8; an index not below the count logs 'Illegal I/O expander index' at level 9 and the code goes on; returns the base plus 16 times the index; read ffe6580c-ffe65860

name: io_expander_name
note: argument 0 is an index byte; takes the 16-byte record from io_expander_record and returns the pointer in its word at +0xc, or the address of the text UNKNOWN when that word is zero; read ffe65864-ffe65890

name: io_expander_state_record
note: argument 0 is an index byte; an index not below the count at 0x300005b8+4 logs 'Illegal I/O expander index' at level 9 and the code goes on; returns the word at 0x300005b8 (a second table base) plus 12 times the index; read ffe65894-ffe658ea

name: io_expander_state_byte3
note: argument 0 is an index byte; returns the byte at offset 3 of the 12-byte record from io_expander_state_record; read ffe658ec-ffe65908

name: io_expander_state_word8
note: argument 0 is an index byte; returns the long at offset 8 of the 12-byte record from io_expander_state_record; read ffe6590c-ffe6592a

name: io_expander_state_byte1
note: argument 0 is an index byte; returns the byte at offset 1 of the 12-byte record from io_expander_state_record, the shadow byte that io_expander_write_bits rewrites; read ffe6592c-ffe6594a

name: io_expander_state_byte0
note: argument 0 is an index byte; returns 0 when the pointer from io_expander_state_record is zero, else the byte at offset 0 of the record, the byte that io_expander_update tests for zero before writing; read ffe6594c-ffe65972

name: io_expander_write_bits
note: arguments: 0 a 16-byte record, 1 the matching 12-byte record, 2 mask byte, 3 value byte; logs at level 9 when the mask overlaps the record byte at +4 and again when the value has bits outside the mask; replaces the shadow byte at 12-byte record +1 with its old value outside the mask ORed with the value; then switches on record byte 0: 0 writes the shadow byte alone to the slave address in record byte +2 with mbus_write_bytes; 1 when the mask overlaps record byte +5 writes the shadow ANDed with byte +5 to register byte +3 with mbus_write_register_bytes and returns a nonzero error, then when the mask has bits outside byte +5 writes byte +4 ORed with the shadow bits outside byte +5 to register byte +3 plus 0x10; 2 writes the shadow byte to register 5; any other type logs at level 1 and returns 0 (so does type 1 when neither write applies); returns the transfer result or 0; read ffe65974-ffe65b3a

name: io_expander_update
note: arguments: 0 index byte, 1 mask byte, 2 value byte; looks up the 16-byte record (io_expander_record) and the 12-byte record (io_expander_state_record) and returns minus 407 when the first byte of the 12-byte record is zero; otherwise runs i2c_bus_acquire with record byte +1 as the bus byte and returns its error when nonzero, else calls io_expander_write_bits with the two records, the mask and the value, then i2c_bus_release, and returns the write result; read ffe65b3c-ffe65bac

name: io_expander_set_bits
note: arguments: 0 index byte, 1 bit byte; calls io_expander_update with the index and the bit byte as both mask and value and returns its result; read ffe65bb0-ffe65bd2

name: io_expander_clear_bits
note: arguments: 0 index byte, 1 bit byte; calls io_expander_update with the index, the bit byte as mask and value 0, and returns its result; read ffe65bd4-ffe65bf0
